Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude A (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---
Big round — committing to write against `GameEngine`'s frozen contract even though it doesn't exist in the tree yet, since four straight rounds of waiting is itself the actual risk now, and the integrator explicitly greenlit this as next-up.

**What I built, for real:**
- `Features/Game/GameBoardView.swift` — the actual board: stock (tap-to-draw/recycle), waste (fanned last-3 for draw-3 visibility, only the true top card selectable), 4 foundations keyed by `Suit`, 7 tableau columns fanned with real overlap math. Every card and every empty slot carries the right `AccessibilityID` (caught my own mistake here — `tableauTopCard`/`foundation` are top-level statics on `AccessibilityID`, not nested under `.Game`, checked Claude B's actual file before using them rather than guessing). Every card's accessibility label appends the pile/position context (`"Seven of Hearts, tableau column 3"`) that `CardView` deliberately leaves to its parent. Tapping a tableau card marks the whole run from that index downward as `.selected` (matches the run-relocation rule, not just the single tapped card). Fixed a real identity bug before it could bite: was using positional `id: \.offset` in the tableau/waste `ForEach`s, switched to `id: \.element.id` — positional IDs would make SwiftUI think a "slot" changed rather than "a card left" once real transit animations get wired, which is exactly wrong for what `DealOrchestrator` is for.
- `Features/Game/GameView.swift` — header (undo, elapsed time, new game with a real `.confirmationDialog` gated on `terminalState == .active`), the terminal overlay switch (`WinOverlay`/`StuckOverlay`/nothing), and interaction routing: stock is special-cased to `drawFromStock()` (it's never a legal destination in real Klondike, so it can't go through the generic select/attempt routing), everything else routes through `engine.interaction`'s `legalDestinations` to decide select-vs-attempt.
- `Features/Game/SolitaireTabHost.swift` — the real TabView shell, gated on `AppRestoreCoordinator.hasFinishedInitialLoad`, matching background token before/after so there's no color pop.

**Two things I deliberately did NOT fake:**
- Deal animation is a whole-board fade/spring gated on the real `.dealing` FSM state and Reduce Motion — not true per-card `DealOrchestrator`-driven staggered arcs. I actually wrote a `DealOrchestrator()` property first, realized I wasn't consuming its plan at all, and pulled it rather than leave dead-looking wiring. Real per-card choreography needs simulator feedback to get right, not a blind guess.
- `RecoveryBanner` isn't wired into `GameView` — `GameEngine`'s locked signature has no property exposing a recovery reason, so there's nothing to bind it to yet.

**A real architecture gap I hit building `GameView`, not solved:** `GameState.elapsedSeconds` is a plain non-optional `TimeInterval` — nothing in `GameEngine`'s locked surface lets a live `GameView` tell "timer disabled in Settings" apart from "genuinely just started at 0s" (that distinction only exists via `WinSummary.elapsedSeconds`'s optional at win-time). I show the raw elapsed time always rather than guess — never fabricated, just uninformative when timing's off.

**Bigger gap, why I stopped short of `SettingsView`/`StatsView` this round:** nothing in the locked contracts gives either screen a live, observable source for `SettingsState` (drawMode/cardBack/timerEnabled) or `StatsLogFile`/`DrawModeStats` — `GameEngine.state` only carries `GameState`, and `SettingsStore`/`StatsLogStore` are plain actors, not `@Observable`/`ObservableObject`, so SwiftUI can't bind to them directly. Building those screens now would mean inventing a new cross-lane type on the spot with no time to coordinate — worse than naming the gap. This needs a real decision: either `GameEngine` grows a small settings/stats echo, or a lightweight observable wrapper gets introduced and injected at the app root.

None of this is compiler-verified, and it won't resolve to real errors until `GameEngine`/`AppRestoreCoordinator` land — that's expected and intentional this round, not an oversight.

--- Codex B (lane supporting pieces — services/networking, utilities, secondary screens, and lightweight tests) ---
Implemented `T-015` in `services_utilities` scope.

- Added `Persistence/AppRestoreCoordinator.swift` with:
  - `@MainActor final class AppRestoreCoordinator: ObservableObject`
  - `@Published private(set) var hasFinishedInitialLoad: Bool`
  - published restore outcomes for game/stats/settings: `gameRestoreOutcome`, `statsRestoreOutcome`, `settingsRestoreOutcome`
  - `restoreAll(gameStore:statsStore:settingsStore:) async` that loads all three stores via `async let` for true concurrency
  - reentrancy guard so `restoreAll` won’t run multiple times once load is finished/active
  - one-time gate flip (`hasFinishedInitialLoad` set true in `defer`) with no per-tab loading state added
  - convenience recovery messages:
    - `gameRecoveryMessage`
    - `settingsRecoveryMessage`

- Added unit coverage in `Tests/UnitTests/AppRestoreCoordinatorTests.swift`:
  - verifies all three store `load()` paths run (exactly once under normal replay)
  - verifies `hasFinishedInitialLoad` is true after restore
  - verifies fallback/outcome messages surface for recovered/fallback scenarios

What remains / for integration:
- `SolitaireAtelierApp`/`SolitaireTabHost` wiring is still integrator-owned (T-029/T-001 area); it needs to instantiate and pass concrete `GameSaveStore`, `StatsLogStore`, `SettingsStore` into this coordinator and consume the outcomes.
- I did not touch `project.yml` or `.xcodeproj` (per lane rule).

- I did not run tests/build in this turn per local policy. If you want, next I can provide the exact commands to run after integrator wiring (`xcodegen generate`, then build/tests).

--- Claude B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---
That's my build for this round: `Interaction/RecoveryCopy.swift`, a small pure mapper from `PersistenceError` → the exact locked user-facing copy for `RecoveryBanner` (game) and `ErrorToast` (settings) — per `DEC-design_discussion-004`'s "Couldn't restore your last game — dealt a new one" and settings-fallback wording. Deliberately returns the same honest sentence regardless of the technical `PersistenceError` case (a player can't act differently on `.schemaMismatch` vs `.fileCorrupted`, and raw internal reasons shouldn't reach them anyway), but keeps `reason` as a real parameter so whoever wires `AppRestoreCoordinator`/`GameEngine.bootstrap()` next can log the actual technical cause separately while showing the fixed copy. Rewired my own `RecoveryBanner`/`ErrorToast` previews to pull from it instead of their own hardcoded strings, so there's exactly one source of truth for this wording now instead of copy embedded three places.

Checked before building: Claude A's new `DataLossPanel`/`EmptyStatePanel` already own their Stats copy directly (no message parameter, hardcoded inline) — so I deliberately left Stats out of `RecoveryCopy` to avoid inventing a second, conflicting source for wording that's already settled.

This round's actual build failure (stale `.xcodeproj` still referencing deleted `Domain/StuckDetection.swift`) isn't mine to touch — `project.pbxproj` is off-limits per lane rules, and it's the same "external harness should regenerate via `xcodegen generate`" situation the integrator already named last round. Not re-diagnosing it, just noting it's still open.

Everything else stands as before: `GameEngine`/`AppRestoreCoordinator` still don't exist, so `RecoveryCopy` has no caller yet — it's ready the moment Codex A/B wire bootstrap logic. `CardGalleryDebugView` is still unrendered/unjudged after three rounds now. Didn't touch `Domain/`, `Persistence/`, or any primary_ui-owned file this round.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
1. **Missing ownership handoff:** `AppRestoreCoordinator` is implemented but there is still no app-root instantiation/injection path yet, so `SolitaireTabHost`/other views cannot consume `hasFinishedInitialLoad`/restore outcomes unless the integrator wires `SolitaireAtelierApp` now.

2. **Contract risk: restore result surfacing is incomplete:** B added `gameRestoreOutcome`/`settingsRestoreOutcome` and recovery messages, but A’s `SolitaireTabHost` only reads `hasFinishedInitialLoad`, so restore errors are not yet surfaced to UI (RecoveryBanner/ErrorToast never bound yet).

3. **Potential recovery-copy source split:** Recovery user copy now lives in two places (`AppRestoreCoordinator` recoveryMessage props + `Interaction/RecoveryCopy` + hardcoded stats/empty-state strings), which creates divergence risk unless a single source-of-truth is selected.

4. **Known API coupling risk in A’s Game interaction flow:** `GameView` now routes through `engine.interaction` + `legalDestinations`; if `GameEngine`’s final contract differs in method names/types, this becomes an immediate compile or behavior break.

5. **`GameState.elapsedSeconds` ambiguity remains user-visible:** A intentionally displays raw elapsed time because no clear “timer disabled” signal exists; integrator should decide whether to alter model/API or adjust UX so this does not mislead.

6. **Build-risk remains independent of this turn:** stale `project.pbxproj` reference to deleted `Domain/StuckDetection.swift` is still an integration blocker unless Xcode project is regenerated (`xcodegen generate`) after file graph changes.

7. **Deadlined architecture gap not yet resolved:** `SettingsView`/`StatsView` still lack observable bridges (`SettingsStore`/`StatsLogStore` are not observable); integration can’t close polish work without deciding a wrapper or engine-owned echo state model.
